final_candidates.decision_summary: Conservative charge-preserving substitution with the strongest combined support: PLM 0.93 and the only positive ProteinMPNN delta, indicating the Arg is structurally preferred. Low functional-annotation risk; best proxy for a tolerable gain in G-mediated entry efficiency.
Aromatic packing retained while removing the hydroxyl; strong PLM (0.91) and good structure compatibility (0.82). Weakly positive MSA (z=0.2) and no annotated functional role.
Highest PLM plausibility (1.0) with acceptable structure compatibility (0.77); conservative charge-preserving change. No homolog support, so confidence is moderate.

stop_reason.detail: Phenotype predictor is unavailable and all applicable evidence tools have been exhausted on the candidate pool; the Top-3 is stable.

history.rationale: N411 sits in an N-N-T sequon near the receptor-binding head; removing an N-glycan at this site can improve ephrinB2/B3 access without disrupting the backbone.

Glycosylation-site addition (N411Q creates NXT/NXS consensus with downstream T/S) may improve folding, stability and receptor-independent trafficking, indirectly boosting entry. Needs structural/evolutionary checks.
ESM-1v strongly disfavors N411Q (z=0.32) and no homolog shows Q at 411 despite the best MSA coverage. Demoted despite receptor-proximity hypothesis.
Weakest combined evidence; kept only as pool filler.
E509 lies adjacent to the aromatic Y511 in the receptor-binding surface; neutralizing its negative charge may reduce electrostatic repulsion at the G-ephrin interface.
Stem-domain charge-neutralizing mutation near heptad-region; plausible stability effect, but reward relevance unproven.
Moderate PLM plausibility (0.71) but no evolutionary support. Retained mid-tier pending structure compatibility.
Balanced evidence (PLM 0.71, structure 0.76, amide-for-acid keeps H-bonding capacity) but MSA shows no homolog support; retained just below R519K.
Y511 is likely part of the hydrophobic pocket engaging the ephrinB2 GH-loop proline; Y-to-F preserves aromatic stacking while subtly altering H-bonding.
Conservative aromatic substitution preserving packing; low risk but unclear entry benefit.
Highest combined support: strong PLM (0.91) and the only mutation with nonzero homolog frequency (0.2 among 5). Conservative aromatic-to-aromatic change suitable for head-region stabilization.
Conserved-tyrosine-to-Phe retains aromatic packing while removing the OH; strong PLM (0.91) and good structure compatibility (0.82) support tolerability. MSA z=0.2 is weakly positive.
D512 borders the pocket; mutation to glycine may increase local backbone flexibility for better induced fit with the receptor loop.
Flexibility-increasing stem mutation; speculative for F-triggering interface.
Perfect PLM score but glycine in a beta strand risks local backbone disruption; needs structure_compatibility check before promoting.
ProteinMPNN strongly disfavors Gly here (ΔlogP=-5.38, normalized 0.11) despite PLM 0.91; the fixed-backbone evidence suggests the Gly would destabilize the receptor-binding domain fold.

rejection.reason: ProteinMPNN strongly disfavors Gly here (ΔlogP=-5.38, normalized 0.11) despite PLM 0.91; the fixed-backbone evidence suggests the Gly would destabilize the receptor-binding domain fold.

history.rationale: N427 (N-T-C sequon) is another predicted N-glycosylation site; glycan pruning in the head domain has been reported to enhance fusion/entry in henipaviruses.
Potential glycosylation motif modification; must verify motif context and viability.
Moderate PLM (0.59) but zero homolog support with good coverage; retained below Y511F.
Moderate PLM and structure scores but no direct entry-efficiency rationale; retained below the leaders.
N459 (N-Q-T sequon) glycan removal could reduce steric shielding of the receptor-binding face.
Glycosylation-adjacent candidate; needs evidence before ranking higher.
Weak-moderate PLM (0.45) and no evolutionary support. Kept as backup only.
Similar profile to N427Q — plausible but not top-3.
Q530 is at the C-terminal edge of the head; introducing positive charge may strengthen contacts with the acidic ephrin receptor surface.
CT-tail charge change; uncertain effect on G trafficking/F interplay.
Good PLM (0.85) but near-zero MSA applicability (2/21 homologs) limits the evolutionary signal. Charge gain may affect receptor-binding surface.
PLM 0.86 and structure 0.88 are good, but very low MSA coverage/applicability (0.10) means evolutionary support is unknown; also a gain of positive charge at high-B-factor site.
K521 is in the receptor-proximal region; conservative K-to-R retains positive charge while potentially improving packing.
Conservative basic-preservation; low risk, low expected gain.
Strong PLM (0.93) for a conservative charge-preserving substitution; weak MSA applicability limits corroboration.
Best combined evidence: PLM 0.93 and the only positive ProteinMPNN delta (+0.53, normalized 0.94), indicating the Arg is structurally preferred at this site. Charge-conserving, low functional risk.
Conservative charge-preserving substitution at an interface-adjacent position, candidate for improved side-chain geometry with ephrinB2.
Conservative; weak prior for entry improvement.
Perfect PLM for a very conservative K/R swap; low risk to viability but uncertain entry benefit.
Highest PLM score (1.0) and acceptable structure compatibility (0.77); conservative charge-preserving change with plausible entry-efficiency rationale.
Surface lysine near the C-terminal head region; arginine may form additional bidentate interactions with acidic receptor residues.
Conservative tail mutation, low expected effect; will be dropped if better candidates emerge.
Both PLM (0.53) and MSA offer little support and no entry-efficiency rationale. Dropped to free a slot.

rejection.reason: Both PLM (0.53) and MSA offer little support and no entry-efficiency rationale. Dropped to free a slot.
